To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the formation of coalitions depends on the environmental interdependence between countries; (ii) large coalitions are formed when the environmental interdependence is low and/or when the damage functions are near separable; (iii) transfers can induce countries to join large coalitions, even in the absence of environmental interdependence.

(1) the formation of a coalition of cooperating countries is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a successful international environmental agreement; (2) transfers can be used to expand such coalitions; (3) large coalitions are possible when environmental interdependence is small; and (4) environmental agreements can be successful even if countries behave as non-cooperative players.
